note: The request-scoped runtime preserves leader-read flags while probing the cached leader and alternate voter peers, and explicitly rejects follower, mixed, learner, stale, and proxy policies. TiFlash and the broader access-mode index remain external.
API-v1 lookup keys and TiKV current-region boundaries cross one explicit memcomparable encode/decode boundary. Keyspace-v2 codecs, scans, and split RPCs remain external.

Ordered lookup, exact observed-route validation, known-leader update, deferred no-leader invalidation, epoch-ahead retry, and atomic split/merge replacement execute through the sole RegionCache authority. Returned current regions are accepted as the available sibling subset, matching client-go without inventing full-coverage requirements. TTL, buckets, background refresh, production concurrency, and broad batch loading remain external.

The request-scoped selector validates canonical store generations on every dispatch, tries the PD leader first, gives a newly elected exhausted peer one fresh attempt, then probes each admissible alternate voter once under unchanged leader-read flags. Per-peer attempts and cumulative RPC time are bounded before exact-region reload. Follower, mixed, learner, stale, prefer-leader, forwarding, busy scoring, and short-read fast rotation remain external.

The bounded selector accounts exact completed RPC time per peer but does not yet consult slow scores. Sliding windows, health scoring, busy fallback, and configurable short-read rotation remain external.

A sorted region vector preserves source key order, half-open containment, and the pre-delete stale-overlap guard that protects newer split children from stale parents. B-tree concurrency, TTL traversal, batch ascent, and benchmarks remain external.

RegionCache owns one canonical store registry shared by every region snapshot. Exact-generation send failure records foreground gRPC liveness and atomically advances a non-reachable store to NeedCheck so later cached regions cannot dispatch through the stale address; stale completions cannot invalidate a newer generation. Health scoring, TLS probes, background refresh/recovery, and production concurrency remain external.
